sections.title: 1. The memory math: why one GPU is not enough

keyTerms.definition: Weights, gradients, optimizer states, activations; training needs all four.
Extra numbers per parameter, like Adam's running averages.
Forward-pass intermediates saved for the backward pass.

recall.question: What is training memory?
recall.answer: Not the model: four piles (weights, gradients, optimizer states, activations) all on GPU at once. Inference needs only weights.

keyTerms.definition: Every GPU holds a full model copy; each trains on a different data slice.
Distributed Data Parallel: PyTorch's implementation; gradients averaged every step.

recall.question: How do DDP replicas stay identical?
recall.answer: After every step, GPUs average their gradients so all copies stay identical.

sections.title: 3. ZeRO: sharding the optimizer, gradients, and weights

keyTerms.definition: Zero Redundancy Optimizer: shards optimizer states, gradients, weights across ranks.
Split into pieces, one piece per GPU; per-GPU memory shrinks as GPUs grow.

recall.question: What redundancy does ZeRO remove?
recall.answer: DDP's full duplication of optimizer state, gradients, and weights on every GPU.

keyTerms.definition: Fully Sharded Data Parallel: PyTorch's native ZeRO-3-style training.
Rewrite on DTensor: per-parameter sharding instead of flattened.
Shards all-gathered just before a unit runs, freed right after.

recall.question: How does FSDP handle parameters?
recall.answer: Flattens each unit's parameters, shards across ranks, all-gathers before the unit runs, frees after.

keyTerms.definition: Splits individual weight matrices across GPUs; Megatron-LM design.
Combines partial results; paid on every layer.

recall.question: When is sharding data not enough?
recall.answer: When a single layer will not fit; then split the layer itself across GPUs.

keyTerms.definition: Cuts the model by layers into stages; microbatches flow like an assembly line.
A batch split so stages stay busy.
The origin schedule versus 1F1B.

recall.question: What are the two schedules?
recall.answer: GPipe versus 1F1B for pipelining microbatches through stages.

keyTerms.definition: Shards the sequence itself: 128k tokens as 16k on each of 8 GPUs.
Attention needs them across the split; the amber arrow is the problem.

recall.question: Which pile did chapters 2-6 leave untouched?
recall.answer: Activations, which explode when contexts get long.

keyTerms.definition: Data, tensor, and pipeline at once; degrees d*t*p = N.
Each GPU's role is a coordinate like 'data rank 2, tensor rank 5, pipeline stage 1'.

recall.question: What is the 3D recipe?
recall.answer: Factor the fleet into a mesh with data, tensor, pipeline degrees multiplying to N.

keyTerms.definition: Complete training snapshot to durable storage; resume instead of restart.
Saves without pausing training; copies to host RAM first.
How often you save, how fast, failure detection, bit-identical resume.

recall.question: What does fault tolerance cover?
recall.answer: Save frequency, save speed, failure detection, and bit-identical resume.
